about: Registers a function reads on some path, found by reading the code not to matter, where the automatic test can't decide (lift.py independence). Each says why. analyse.py stops counting them as inputs, as for independent.json. Entries marked 'reviewed' came from an independent review (2026-11-05): one analyst argued the case from the instructions, three skeptics each tried to find an input where the value matters, and an entry was kept only if none could. 'condition' is any input under which it would matter, which no caller in the game passes.

func_800007D4.why: The game's memory allocator (best fit over the free list at 0x800435F0). In the loop it sets a3 (the best block so far) and s1 (the block before it) together, at 0x8000088C and 0x80000890. On the way out, s1 is copied to s0 (0x800008B0) in the delay slot of `beq $v1, $zero` (0x800008AC, v1 = a3), and s0 is only used when that branch isn't taken, that is when a3 was set, and so s1 with it. When no block was found, s0 is restored from the stack unused. The random-input tester can't show this: random memory turns the free list into loops.

func_8002985C.why: The sound system's voice allocator: a free voice of the 0x13C-byte ones at 0x8008D290, or else the lowest-priority one. a2 starts one above the new sound's priority (s2) and drops to a voice's priority only together with s1 becoming that voice. s1 is used only if a2 ends up below s2, which needs that to have happened. The one exception is s2 = 0x7FFFFFFF, where s2 + 1 wraps: a sound priority of that size isn't plausible, and the original would then use whatever s1 held as a voice pointer.

func_8012C474.why: s2 is set to the wrestler slot (0x358 bytes each at 0x8016F7E0) when an element's slot number is below 0x64, and only used later in the same loop pass under the same test of the same element. The calls between the two tests aren't given a pointer to the element list (a local array), so the number can't change between them.

s7.argument:
s3 is the pass counter. It is set to 0 at 0x8013C5B8. The only place it changes is 0x8013C7CC (s3 += 1), and that is followed by 0x8013C7D0/0x8013C7D4, which loop back to L_8013C5E8 only while s3 < 4. So inside the body s3 is always 0, 1, 2 or 3, and it is never negative. Pass s3 == 0 takes the collect path at 0x8013C5E8 (bne not taken) and jumps to L_8013C7C0 at 0x8013C678. That path never touches s7, so every s7 read is inside the sort loop (L_8013C68C..L_8013C7B8), where s3 is 1, 2 or 3.

Two values the sort loop tests stay fixed:
- fp = 3, set at 0x8013C5C0. fp is never written again in the function, and the callees (0x8000AEC8, 0x80137160, 0x8000AEE8) must preserve it because it is callee-saved.
- a2 = (s3 < 3), set at 0x8013C688. The sort loop makes no calls and never writes a2.

The reads:
(1) 0x8013C738 and 0x8013C744 come right after the sets at 0x8013C730 (lh s7,0(a0)) and 0x8013C740 (lh s7,8(a0)), so they read the newly loaded value. 0x8013C728 is the delay slot of the j at 0x8013C724 and comes after the set at 0x8013C720 (lh s7,6(a0)), so it also reads the new value.
(2) 0x8013C700 is the delay slot of `beq s3,a3(=1),L_8013C71C` at 0x8013C6FC. To get there: s3 != 2 (0x8013C6EC not taken) and a2 != 0, i.e. s3 < 3 (0x8013C6F4 not taken). With s3 in {1,2,3}, that leaves only s3 == 1, so the beq at 0x8013C6FC is always taken. The v0 computed at 0x8013C700 from the entry s7 is overwritten at 0x8013C728, after s7 is set at 0x8013C720, and nothing reads v0 in between. The fall-through 0x8013C704 (j L_8013C748), which would carry that stale v0 to the test at 0x8013C748, needs s3 to be outside {1,2} with 0 < s3 < 3. No such s3 exists.
(3) 0x8013C710 is the delay slot of `beq s3,fp(=3),L_8013C73C` at 0x8013C70C. To get there: s3 != 2 and a2 == 0, i.e. s3 >= 3, so s3 == 3, and the beq is always taken. The v0 computed at 0x8013C710 is overwritten at 0x8013C744, after s7 is set at 0x8013C740, with no read in between. The fall-through 0x8013C714 needs s3 >= 4, which the loop bound at 0x8013C7D0 rules out whatever arg0 is (the exit test at 0x8013C7C4 can only end the loop sooner).

So the entry value of s7 never reaches the swap decision at 0x8013C748, any memory address or stored value, any call argument, or v0/v1. The only other use is the save at 0x8013C5C8 (sw s7,0x3C(sp)). That slot is never written again (the only other frame store is a0 to 0x14(sp) at 0x8013C5E4), and it is loaded back into s7 at 0x8013C7E4, so this is just the callee-saved save and restore. m2c's `var_v0 = var_s4 < var_s7` in the 'empty' branches stands for those dead delay-slot computations, and those branches cannot be reached.
s7.what_it_does: On pass 0 it collects every qualifying entry ID into the byte list at *0x800F6130 (count in s5). Passes 1-3 (up to arg0) then sort that list in place, comparing the signed halfword at offset 6, 0 or 8 of each list entry's 10-byte record in the table at *0x800F612C. It returns the count.

s5.argument:
Control structure: s3 is set to 0 at 0x8013C5B8. Only two edges reach L_8013C5E8: the fall-through from entry (s3 = 0) and the back-edge at 0x8013C7D4. That back-edge is taken only after s3 is incremented at 0x8013C7CC, and only while s3 < 4 (0x8013C7D0). s3 only grows (0, 1, 2, 3) and is never written anywhere else, so the s3 == 0 pass runs exactly once, as the very first pass, and every path from entry goes through it.

First pass (s3 = 0): the bne at 0x8013C5E8 is not taken. Its delay slot at 0x8013C5EC reads the ENTRY s5 into s1 (s1 = s5 - 2). The next instruction, 0x8013C5F0, sets s5 = 0, and 0x8013C5F4 sets s1 = 0 before s1 is read anywhere. So the only read of the entry value is overwritten without ever being used. From 0x8013C5F0 on, s5 is a counter starting at 0. In the inner loop it is read at 0x8013C640 (index for the store at 0x8013C648) and at 0x8013C644 (s5 += 1). Both come after 0x8013C5F0 on every path. The three callees (0x8000AEC8, 0x80137160, 0x8000AEE8) must preserve s5 under the ABI. The pass ends with j L_8013C7C0 at 0x8013C678, so s5 then holds the count of entries stored.

Exit or loop-back at L_8013C7C0: v0 = s5 at 0x8013C7C8 (delay slot of the beq at 0x8013C7C4) and at 0x8013C7D8 (delay slot of the bne at 0x8013C7D4). Both are reached only after the first pass, so both read the defined count, not the entry value.

Later passes (s3 = 1, 2, 3): the branch at 0x8013C5E8 is taken. Its delay slot at 0x8013C5EC computes s1 = count - 2, and 0x8013C69C computes s0 = count - 1. Both use s5 as set in the first pass, because no instruction on the s3 != 0 paths (0x8013C680 to 0x8013C7B8) writes s5.

Restore: 0x8013C7EC reloads s5 from 0x34(sp), the slot saved at 0x8013C5D0. That restores the saved value, which does not count as an output. No sp-relative store touches that slot; the only one is 0x8013C5E4 (a0 to 0x14(sp)).

So every read of s5 except 0x8013C5EC in the first pass sees a value set at 0x8013C5F0 or 0x8013C644. The one entry-value read (0x8013C5EC) goes into s1, which 0x8013C5F4 overwrites before any use. The entry s5 cannot affect any memory write, call argument, v0 or v1, for any input. This leaves aside the absurd case where the global byte buffer at *(0x800F6130) points into this function's own save area; that would be stack aliasing, not a data path from the register.
s5.what_it_does: On the first pass it builds a byte list at *(0x800F6130) from 12 groups, keeping the items that func_8000AEC8/func_80137160 accept (values from func_8000AEE8) and counting them in s5. Passes 1 to 3, up to and including the pass equal to arg0, then sort that list by halfword field 0x6, 0x0 or 0x8 of 10-byte records at *(0x800F612C). It returns the count.

s4.argument:
s3 can only be 0, 1, 2 or 3. It is set to 0 at 0x8013C5B8. Its only change is the +1 at 0x8013C7CC. The loop goes back to L_8013C5E8 only while s3 < 4 (0x8013C7D0/0x8013C7D4); the other exit is the beq at 0x8013C7C4. s3 is callee-saved, so the calls at 0x8013C618/0x8013C620/0x8013C630 cannot change it. fp is set to 3 at 0x8013C5C0 and is only reloaded at 0x8013C7E0, and the callees must preserve it.

When s3 == 0, the bne at 0x8013C5E8 is not taken. That path (0x8013C5F0-0x8013C67C) never touches s4 and ends with j L_8013C7C0. So all the code that reads s4 (L_8013C68C onward) runs only when s3 is 1, 2 or 3. In that code, a2 = (s3 < 3) is set once at 0x8013C688, before the L_8013C68C loop. Nothing between there and 0x8013C7B8 changes a2, and that range makes no calls.

There are two early reads of s4 at 0x8013C700 and 0x8013C710. Neither can affect anything:
- s3 == 1: the beq at 0x8013C6EC (a3=2) is not taken, and neither is the beq at 0x8013C6F4 (a2=1). The beq at 0x8013C6FC (a3=1 from 0x8013C6F8) is taken. Its delay slot 0x8013C700 computes v0 = s4<s7, which may use the entry s4. Execution then reaches L_8013C71C, which reloads s4 (0x8013C71C) and s7 (0x8013C720), and the delay slot 0x8013C728 overwrites v0 before the beql at 0x8013C748 reads it.
- s3 == 3: the beq at 0x8013C6EC is not taken. The beq at 0x8013C6F4 is taken (a2=0), and so is the beq at 0x8013C70C (s3 == fp == 3). Its delay slot 0x8013C710 computes v0 from the entry s4, but 0x8013C73C/0x8013C740 reload s4 and s7 and 0x8013C744 overwrites v0.
- s3 == 2: the branch at 0x8013C6EC goes to 0x8013C72C, which sets s4 before the read at 0x8013C738.
- The fall-through jumps at 0x8013C704 and 0x8013C714 are the only routes that would let the stale v0 from 0x8013C700/0x8013C710 reach 0x8013C748. They need s3 to be outside {1,2} with s3<3 (0x8013C704), or s3>=3 with s3 != 3 (0x8013C714). Neither can happen when s3 is 1, 2 or 3, so both jumps are dead.

The other reads come after a write on every path:
- 0x8013C728 follows the write at 0x8013C71C.
- 0x8013C738 follows the write at 0x8013C72C.
- 0x8013C744 follows the write at 0x8013C73C.
- 0x8013C778 (sb s4) follows the write at 0x8013C764 (lbu s4) in the same straight-line block.

The entry s4 never reaches a call either. Calls happen only on the s3==0 path, and their arguments come from s1/s0/v0 (0x8013C614, 0x8013C61C, 0x8013C624, 0x8013C62C, 0x8013C634). No stack arguments are written.

At exit, s4 is restored at 0x8013C7F0 from 0x30(sp), which was saved at 0x8013C5D4. The only other stack store is a0 to 0x14(sp) at 0x8013C5E4, so the saved value is intact. The m2c C, where var_v0 = var_s4 < var_s7 sits in branches that can't be reached, matches this analysis.

The entry value of s4 can never affect a memory write, call argument, v0/v1 result, or the restore of a callee-saved register, for any inputs.
s4.what_it_does: On pass s3=0 it collects IDs into the byte array at *(0x800F6130), keeping those that func_80137160 accepts across 12 groups (counts in halfwords at 0x800A99B4 + 0x38*i). On passes s3=1..3, up to the a0 limit, it sorts that array with a swap-sort keyed on the halfword at offset 6, 0 or 8 of 10-byte records at *(0x800F612C). It returns the count in v0.

fp.argument:
The function never reads the entry value of fp. Every path to each of the three reads sets fp first, and nothing writes fp between that set and the read.

Reaching the region: the only way into 0x8013B864..0x8013B8D8 is to fall through from 0x8013B864. Every branch in the loop body (0x8013B65C..0x8013B860) targets a label at or below 0x8013B864. The early exit at 0x8013B630 jumps to L_8013B954, past the whole region. No instruction before 0x8013B878 writes fp, and none reads it except the save at 0x8013B600, `sw fp,0x48(sp)`.

Read at 0x8013B880 (`lb fp,-0x7EA8(fp)`): this is the delay slot of `j` at 0x8013B87C, so it runs right after `lui fp,0x8016` at 0x8013B878. The base it reads is always 0x80160000, which the function set itself. The load then overwrites fp with the signed byte at 0x80158158.

Read at 0x8013B8C8 (`bltz fp`): three edges reach it.
(a) The `j` at 0x8013B87C, taken when func_801091F0 returns 2 (the branch at 0x8013B870 falls through). fp was set at 0x8013B878 and 0x8013B880.
(b) The `bne v1,zero` at 0x8013B89C. v1 is set to 0 in the delay slot at 0x8013B890, which always runs. If the byte at 0x80158158 is >= 0, the branch at 0x8013B88C falls through to 0x8013B894, which sets fp to v0, and 0x8013B898 sets v1 to 1. So v1 != 0 at 0x8013B89C only when fp was set at 0x8013B894. If the byte is < 0, the branch at 0x8013B88C jumps straight to 0x8013B89C with v1 = 0, so the branch is not taken.
(c) Arriving at 0x8013B8C0 (`beql v1,zero`). That label is reached either from the taken `bltz` at 0x8013B8B0 or by falling through from 0x8013B8BC. Along the taken edge v1 is still 0, since only v0 is written at 0x8013B8A4..0x8013B8AC. The beql is then taken and its likely delay slot at 0x8013B8C4 sets fp to -1. Along the fall-through, 0x8013B8B8 set fp to v0 and 0x8013B8BC set v1 to 1, so the beql is not taken and the next instruction, 0x8013B8C8, sees the fp from 0x8013B8B8.
On every edge, fp at 0x8013B8C8 is a value this function loaded or set. The path-insensitive analysis missed the link between v1 and fp: v1 = 1 exactly when fp has been set.

Read at 0x8013B8D8 (`addiu v1,fp,1`): it is only reached by falling through from 0x8013B8C8. The delay slot 0x8013B8CC and the instructions at 0x8013B8D0 and 0x8013B8D4 do not write fp, so this read sees the same value the function set.

After that, fp is not used until 0x8013B95C (`lw fp,0x48(sp)`), which restores the entry value saved at 0x8013B600. The function stores to its own frame only at 0x8013B628 (0x14(sp)) and in the register saves, so nothing overwrites the 0x48(sp) slot. No call receives a pointer into the frame: func_801091F0 takes no meaningful arguments, func_800D9AB0 gets a0=8, a1 = the halfword at 0x801507E4+s5, a2=0, a3=0x801507E4, and func_800E3664 takes none. The early-exit path through L_8013B954 also leads straight to this restore.

The entry fp is therefore only saved and restored unchanged, which by the stated rules is not an output. For any parameters, memory contents or callee results, it cannot affect a memory write, a call argument, v0, v1, f0 or f1. The one exception would need a game global such as 0x80159214 to point into this function's own stack frame, so that slot accesses alias the saved-register slots. That is memory aliasing of the save slot, not a read of the fp register, and it does not involve the flagged instructions.

The m2c line `var_fp = saved_reg_fp` is an artifact of the same path-insensitivity: every branch of the if/else at C lines 116-135 assigns var_fp before line 137.
fp.what_it_does: It rebuilds an 8-entry table of wrestler slots, starting at the pointer stored at 0x80159214 and stepping 0x88 bytes per slot, from the 6-byte entries at 0x801507E0. It then picks a slot index from 0x80158158 or ((*0x8015B928)+1), or uses -1, finds the matching slot, stores that index (or 0) to 0x80159204, and returns 0xC or the original a0.

s4.argument: s4's entry value is never read as data. It is only saved and restored. 1) At 0x801303DC s5 is set to 0. No branch or call comes between that and the loop head L_8013045C. s5 is changed only at 0x80130560 (the likely-branch delay slot, run only when taken) and 0x8013058C, both near the end of the loop body. 2) So on the first trip through the loop, beq s5,zero at 0x8013045C is always taken, to L_80130474. 0x80130474 sets s4 = 1 before any read of s4. The fall-through path (0x80130464-0x80130470), which skips that set, can only run when s5 != 0, which means on the second trip. 3) The reads come after 0x80130474 in program order: 0x80130524 is in the inner loop L_80130498, reached through 0x80130488; 0x80130558 is reached through 0x8013054C; 0x8013056C and 0x80130580 are in loop L_80130568. On the first trip all of them run after s4 = 1. The only way back to L_8013045C is the bne at 0x80130594, which is reached only after a first trip that executed 0x80130474. So on the second trip (s5 = 1), s4 holds 1 plus the increments from 0x80130524 and 0x8013056C, not the entry value. 4) The jal func_8010791C at 0x801304B4 runs only after 0x80130474. s4 is callee-saved, so whatever the callee does, the value it leaves belongs to this function, not to the caller's entry value. 5) The entry value is used only in the save at 0x801303F0 (sw s4,0x20(sp), in this function's own frame) and the restore at 0x801305B0 (lw s4,0x20(sp)) just before jr ra at 0x801305CC. That is the standard callee-saved save and restore, which does not count as an output. No input, however unlikely, can make a read see the entry value: s5 = 0 on the first trip is unconditional. m2c's 'var_s4 = saved_reg_s4' is a path-insensitive artifact; it is overwritten by 'var_s4 = 1' in the s5 == 0 branch, which is always taken first.
s4.what_it_does: Two passes (s5 = 0, then s5 = 1) over 0x88-byte entries starting after the pointer stored at 0x80158FA4. For the active entries counted by the halfwords at 0x800A958A and 0x800A958C, it calls func_8010791C and sets IDs (0x1320+i or 0x13A0+i) and float grid positions. It then sets bit 0 of the halfword at entry offset 0x4A and zeroes the halfword at offset 0x60 for the remaining entries, up to 6 or 17.

f20.argument:
The only read of f20 is c.le.s $f0,$f20 at 0x8012BF0C (inside the loop L_8012BF00). f20 is set only by the a1 dispatch:
- a1==1: beq at 0x8012BE6C goes to L_8012BEBC, where 0x8012BEC4 sets f20=56.5685.
- a1==0: slti at 0x8012BE74 gives 1, so the beql at 0x8012BE78 is not taken. beq at 0x8012BE80 goes to L_8012BEA8, where 0x8012BEB0 sets f20=43.8406.
- a1==2: beql at 0x8012BE78 is taken (its delay slot sets v0=2). beq at 0x8012BE90 goes to L_8012BED4, where 0x8012BEDC sets f20=73.5391.
- a1==3: falls to 0x8012BE98, which goes to L_8012BEEC. 0x8012BEF4 sets f20=127.279.
- Every other a1 skips all four writes. A negative a1 goes through 0x8012BE80 (not taken), its delay slot 0x8012BE84 sets s0=0, then j at 0x8012BE88. An a1 of 4 or more goes through 0x8012BE98 (not taken), its delay slot 0x8012BE9C sets s0=0, then j at 0x8012BEA0. Both reach L_8012BEF8 with f20 still holding its entry value.
On that path the loop runs from 0x8012BF00. It calls func_8012EA74 (a0=s1, starting at 0x8014D1A8, a1=s2=arg0), then compares f0<=f20 at 0x8012BF0C. If true, bc1t at 0x8012BF18 exits with v0=s0, set in its delay slot at 0x8012BF1C. If false, it increments s0, adds 0xC to s1, and loops up to 4 times (0x8012BF20-0x8012BF2C), then sets v0=-1 at 0x8012BF30. So the entry f20 decides the return value v0 (0..3 or -1). It also decides how many more calls to func_8012EA74 are made, and with which a0. That is observable whenever a1 is outside {0,1,2,3}. The ldc1 at 0x8012BF44 only restores the value saved at 0x8012BE68, which does not count.
Reachability in the game: the ROM holds exactly 9 jal instructions to 0x8012BE50 (0x0C04AF94). I matched them to the 9 call sites in the disassembly. Every one loads a1 with a constant in its delay slot or just before the call:
- func_800E873C: a1=0
- func_8010FF78: a1=2 and a1=0
- func_80110D7C: a1=2 and a1=0
- func_8011F8D8: a1=3
- func_80129128: a1=1
- func_801297E0: a1=1, set at line 117 and not changed before the jal
- func_8013E280: a1=1
The word 0x8012BE50 does not appear anywhere in the ROM, so nothing calls the function through a pointer. In the game a1 is always 0..3, so f20 is always set before 0x8012BF0C and the entry value never matters.
f20.condition: a1 (arg1) not in {0,1,2,3}, meaning a1 < 0 or a1 >= 4. Then f20 keeps its entry value. At 0x8012BF0C that value is compared with func_8012EA74's f0, and the result decides the return value (0..3 or -1) and how many calls are made to func_8012EA74. All 9 real call sites pass 0, 1, 2 or 3.
f20.what_it_does: Picks a distance threshold from arg1 (0..3: 43.84, 56.57, 73.54, 127.28). It then calls func_8012EA74 for each of 4 entries 12 bytes apart, starting at 0x8014D1A8, passing arg0. It returns the index of the first entry whose result is at or below the threshold, or -1 if none is.

t9.argument:
Where t9 is set. Only two blocks set t9 from constants: L_80147500 (0x80147500 lui, then 0x80147508 addiu in the delay slot of the non-likely bne at 0x80147504, so it always runs) gives t9 = 0x80150EF0, and L_8014752C (0x8014752C/0x80147530) gives t9 = 0x80150F70. After that, t9 only steps forward by 4 at 0x801475DC (delay slot of 0x801475D8, so it always runs). The back edges at 0x801475D8 (to L_801475C4), 0x80147984 (to L_801475C0) and 0x801479E8 (to L_801475A8) all go to code after the setters and never reload t9. So once t9 is set, every later read sees a value built from one of those constants.

The branch that decides it. Every path to the reads goes through L_801474C0. At 0x801474C0, bnel t2 jumps to L_801479F4 (the exit) when t2 != 0. That path stores t8 and a0, restores registers and returns without touching t9. When t2 == 0, 0x801474D8 does lbu v1, 0x10(a2), with a2 = t3*20 + t0 (0x801474C8-0x801474D4). lbu zero-extends, so v1 is 0..255 and bltz at 0x801474DC is never taken. Then:
- v1 < 2: bne at 0x801474E4 goes to L_80147500, which sets t9.
- 2 <= v1 < 4: 0x801474F0 falls through to j L_8014752C at 0x801474F8, which sets t9.
- v1 >= 4: beq at 0x801474F0 jumps to L_80147574. Its delay slot (0x801474F4) only sets s0 = 0, and t9 is never set.

What happens when v1 >= 4. At 0x80147574-0x80147588 the same address is computed again (t3 and t0 have not changed) and its byte goes into t7 (0x801475A4), so t7 >= 4. The loop then reaches 0x801475C4, lw v1, 0(t9), with t9 still holding its entry value. 0x801475D0 stores the low byte of that word to a3 + a2 + 0xC, where a3 = a0 = *arg1 (0x801472F4, 0x801475B4). With t7 >= 4, the type tests at 0x801475E0, 0x801476BC, 0x80147798 and 0x80147880 all branch past the drawing code, so only sh zero at 0x80147884 runs. The loops repeat this 2 x 4 x 4 times: 32 loads from entry_t9 + 0, 4, ..., 0x7C, and their low bytes go to bytes 0xC-0xF of each 16-byte vertex in the buffer at *arg1. The address of the load and the stored values both depend on the entry t9, so on this path the entry value is observable (memory writes, or a fault on a bad address).

Why v1 >= 4 can't happen in the game. The byte is a type field with four values: 0..3.
- The code handles only t7 = 0..3 (0x801475E0, 0x801476BC, 0x80147798, 0x80147880).
- The table at 0x80151070 that 0x801475A0 indexes holds 4 pointers (0x80150FF0 x2, 0x80151030 x2); what follows is not pointers (0, 0, 3, 0).
- The two t9 tables are exactly 0x80 bytes each, the 32 words the loops read.

I read the ROM (ovl_c: rom 0xAE390 <-> vram 0x80106760). What the entry value would change if it got through:

- Read 2, 0x80106F98. This is the delay slot of a bnel, so it runs only when that byte != 0 and the loop's s2 < s3. Then s3 -= entry s4, so the value stored to 0x8015C904 at 0x80106FB8 depends on entry s4.

Why that cannot happen in the game:

Every path A route then goes 0x80147AC4 -> L_80147DAC with t0 already set, so path A never reads the entry t0.

Each block sets t0 with lui (B54, BA8, BFC, C50, CA4, CF8, D4C, DA0) before its reads (B58/B5C/B64 ... DA4/DA8). Each block ends with `j L_80147DB0` (or falls from DA8 into DAC), so none falls into the next block. Those reads are therefore safe.

- Where it goes: 0x80147DB0 makes v1 = sext8(t0). 0x80147DB4-DBC multiply it by 80, and 0x80147DC0 adds that to a3. The loads at 0x80147DD8/DEC/E00/E18/E2C/E90 (or E4C/E60/E74/E8C/EA0/EB8) read from a3 + 80*sext8(t0_entry) + offset. IN THE GAME. All callers pass a0 = 0x800A10F8 (func_8010FBE4, func_801264E8, func_80126624). The only writer with callers is func_80130718. When the entrant count N = h[0x800A958A] < 9, it sets unk8 = 0 and unk4 = N. Otherwise it sets unk8 = N/2 and unk4 = N - N/2. So unk8 != 0 means total = N >= 9. - the per-count byte tables (0x80151574..0x80151608) and the case jump table stop at 16;
- the defaults are 16 (0x8012E8CC) and 12 (func_801326E0);

So the unset route needs a bracket of more than 16 entrants.

Not verified: rumble mode stores its own count (4..40) in the same byte, 0x80157EA7, that func_8012E784 reads for the tournament. I did not check whether a stale rumble count of 17 or more can reach N. If this function is translated, keep t0 as a real input on this route (or make the default explicit). 3) 0x80117298 (bnel/beq delay slot after 0x8011728C). Here a1 = 0x80150000 - 0x40A8 = 0x8014BF58 (0x8010DCBC/0x8010DCC0), so the lwl address is 0x8014BF5C. That address is word-aligned (0x5C = 4*23). A big-endian lwl at an aligned address loads all 4 bytes and keeps none of the old register. The following lwr at 0x8010DCD0 (address 0x8014BF5F, byte offset 3) also loads the full word, sign-extended. More generally, an lwl A / lwr A+3 pair writes all 4 bytes for any alignment: lwl writes 4-(A&3) bytes and lwr writes (A&3) bytes, or 4 when A&3 = 0. So after 0x8010DCD0, v1 holds memory contents only, and no entry bits survive. The lwr's read of v1 at 0x8010DCD0 sees the value 0x8010DCCC wrote, not the entry value.
